config.description: The cost curve below 512 tokens, which the model currently extrapolates from the origin, plus a direct measurement of whether decomposing a padded residual into exact bucket sizes wins. Both hinge on the fixed per-step cost, which linear-from-origin assumes is zero and which no dispatch under 512 tokens has ever tested.
config.note_decomposition: 1808 = 1024+512+256+16 exactly, and 1808 pads to 2048. On the extrapolated curve decomposition wins by 1.85 ms; that depends entirely on C(16)=0.41 ms, which is an assumption. Measured directly here.
config.note_prediction: cost x~1.02 => padding not paid (cost tracks real tokens). cost x~2.0 => padding paid (cost tracks the compiled bucket).
config.note_seq_len: Per-sequence length is near-constant within an edge (128 vs 130) on purpose. Comparing 4x96 against 4x128 would move sequence length by a third, changing attention work materially and destroying the clean prediction that cost is proportional to real tokens.
config.note_single_step: Both edges sit far below max_num_batched_tokens=8192 so the scheduler has no reason to split. Every dispatch records its step count and splits are counted, not averaged over: a split reintroduces exactly the smearing this experiment exists to avoid.
config.note_sizes: Every size is exactly a compiled bucket edge, so these measure REAL cost with zero padding. 512 and 1024 overlap existing knots (13.15 and 17.23 ms) and act as a consistency check on the whole exercise.
